summary: Approved sequence sheets for WX-4 tablets (WA/2015/137) for Wexanthel Medicines: eighteen-month stability pulls, method qualification results, solution preparation and the sequence sheet record. The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend, and Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister. Assay stayed within limits at every pull.

sheets.name: Summary

rows.v: Wexanthel WX-4 tablets: eighteen-month stability and method qualification

rows: Eighteen-month ICH stability of WX-4 tablets with assay and related-substances qualification. Interim review completed 22 Apr 2016.

Assay at time zero was {{PRJ0088:stability.t0_assay}} % label claim. The qualified method detected an impurity trend that depended on the pack. Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister for WX-4 tablets. Conclusions are limited to the tested interval.
Stability results and total impurities chart
Solution preparation and units as written in the batch card

sheets.name: Pulls
rows: Assay as % label claim (HPLC). Impurities as % area. Water by Karl Fischer. The table is organised by storage condition, not by packaging presentation; packaging identities and comparison records remain on the batch card. Time zero is one initial analysis shared by all storage conditions; repeated initial rows do not represent separate pulls.

rows: Qualified against the HPLC method qualification protocol. Acceptance criteria as written in the protocol.

sheets.name: Deviations
rows: Refer to the batch card and approved sequence sheets.
Long-term and intermediate pulls extend to the final reported timepoint; accelerated pulls stop at six months.
Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister following the packaging-dependent impurity trend. The condition table does not quantify that comparison.
